canonical_topic: Eastern Interconnect structure: RTO/ISOs and regulated utilities
definition: The Eastern Interconnect covers the eastern half of the U.S. as a mix of organized RTO/ISO markets and traditionally regulated utilities, and is less geographically constrained than the Western Interconnect.
core_idea: PJM and MISO are the two largest RTO/ISOs in North America, alongside SPP, NYISO, and ISO-NE, with MISO-Indiana Hub and PJM Western Hub standing out as the most liquid trading points in the region.
key_points: Eastern Interconnect is a combination of RTO/ISOs and regulated utilities, less dominated by geography than the West
PJM (originally Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnection) and MISO are the two largest RTO/ISOs in North America
Other RTO/ISOs in the region: SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE
Most liquid trading locations: MISO-Indiana Hub (formerly Cin-Hub/Cinergy Hub) and PJM Western Hub (PJM-W)
trading_implications: Indiana Hub and PJM-W are the reference liquid benchmarks for Eastern Interconnect power trading
caveats: MISO-Indiana Hub is a renamed successor to what was historically called Cin-Hub or Cinergy Hub
